title: QwikLit Editor’s Choice — Reader Review Edition
selectionMethod: Screened all 555 live-feed entries, including 375 dated in the two-month window; excluded misclassified, excerpt-only, and non-literary items. Read full publisher texts of short-story finalists and applied the local ten-characteristic editorial rubric before selection. Checked chosen publisher pages for form, byline, date, and canonical link. The source feed was partial: 70 of 77 publishers refreshed successfully, so retained entries from failed sources may be stale. Lightspeed displays its November issue rather than a day; day-level dates for its two selections follow the live feed.

items.title: Choke, Writhe Perish: A Recipe for Forging a Virgin Sacrifice to Feed the Dragon
items.editorialNote: A grieving woman builds a false sacrifice from the dead and the village’s covert help. The recipe’s ingredients become a plan to bring down both the dragon and the council that feeds it.

items.title: A Map to Sideways Places
items.editorialNote: On a planet that defeats every sense of direction, an expedition guide trusts a giant beetle to lead her tourists through the mist. Their discovery forces her to decide what being lost has given her.

items.title: Something for Nothing
items.editorialNote: A customer in a secondhand shop asks for a skin, and the cashier sees an opportunity for a profitable trade. In a few hundred words, the bargain turns the question of who is using whom inside out.

items.title: The Last Angel in Heaven
items.authorDisplay: Ava Arnejo, translated from Cebuano by shane carreon
items.editorialNote: When a police raid sends a waitress through a student’s window, the two hide together under a bed. The night’s danger and the small acts of shelter make their brief connection linger.

items.title: Migration Season
items.editorialNote: A speaker addresses a body sprouting swans as if it were a fascinating diagnosis. The poem’s clinical curiosity slips into grief, making its surreal imagery both sharp and unsettling.

items.title: First Snow in Berlin
items.editorialNote: Snow settling quietly outside a Berlin window brings back the sound of rain on a Kenyan roof and a mother calling her child to eat. A few exact images hold two kinds of weather and home together.

items.title: The plants remember her on any planet
items.editorialNote: In an off-world greenhouse, starfruit and tomato vines keep the memory of a mother close. The poem lets its imagined technology recede so that a circulating breeze can carry the grief.

items.title: Daughter of the Anthropocene and the Modern Day
items.editorialNote: An alphabet of citrus trees, family dinners, extinction and wonder joins climate-scale time to a single young life. The entries make an abstract crisis intimate without losing their curiosity.

items.title: Dancers Mourning Dolly
items.editorialNote: At a dance held in Dolly Parton’s memory, strangers lead, follow and exchange a few words between songs. Cabrera catches the community in its movement, especially a widow who learned to lead.

items.title: I Found Transitioning Surprisingly Joyful
items.editorialNote: Woods recounts the practical support that made their transition surprisingly straightforward in Vancouver. Their personal experience gives the essay a concrete way to ask what care and safety could look like elsewhere.
